text:
The Avalanche lost their two best players in one week: Nathan MacKinnon is out about a month and Cale Makar about two weeks, the timelines the team announced on Nov. 14. That is the season's story in Denver for now, and so far the rest of the roster has answered, beating Montreal behind Artturi Lehkonen and Mackenzie Blackwood and then the Ducks on Thursday.

The cushion was built before the injuries. Colorado is 13-7-3 with 55% of the expected goals, our measure of the quality of chances, and the MacKinnon line with Lehkonen and Martin Necas had outscored teams 20-10 at 5-on-5. The Avs have also scored about 11 more goals than their chances deserved, finishing that will be harder to keep up without their top scorer.

Brock Nelson now centers Lehkonen and Necas, who took a scary hit against Utah on Wednesday but played Thursday. Nazem Kadri and Gabriel Landeskog form the second line, and a defenseman claimed off waivers after Makar went down made his debut against Anaheim. Devon Toews, Makar's usual partner, now plays with Sam Malinski.

Our playoff odds still give Colorado 96%, and the points earned match the play. What we'd watch over the next month: whether a 6-2-2 team in its last 10 can tread water until its stars come back.
headline: Life without MacKinnon and Makar
